title: Leash Layer
tagline: Revocable ENSv2 authorization and scoped credentials for agent software
description:
Leash is an explainable permission layer for agent software. It identifies an agent wallet
  through ERC-8004, reads its capabilities from ENSv2 on Ethereum Sepolia, and decides whether a requested action is allowed. When approved, Leash issues a short lived, singleuse
  credential scoped to one capability and wallet address. Before the protected service
  executes, authority is checked again against ENSv2, so revoking a role immediately blocks the
  next request. The project demonstrates how agents can receive bounded permissions instead of permanent API access.
how_its_made:
Leash is built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, Bun, and viem. The Next.js dashboard and
  server-side API routes use shared authorization logic from the src backend layer. A custom
  ENSv2 client reads resource ownership, expiry, and role bitmaps from Ethereum Sepolia.
  Capabilities are mapped to required roles, and the gate returns structured ALLOW or DENY
  decisions with stable reason codes, block numbers, and latency. Approved requests receive
  HMAC-signed credentials containing the agent, wallet, capability, expiry, and nonce. The
  protected service validates the credential, prevents reuse, and performs a live ENSv2 re-
  check before execution.
auto_summary: Leash gates agent actions by reading role-based authority from ENSv2 on Sepolia and issuing short-lived single-use credentials.
